title: Development and Validation of the Chinese Care Scale in University Students in Hong Kong
content: Cultivating the virtue of care is vital to university students’ whole-person development and benefits society as a whole. However, a culturally appropriate, particularly for Chinese university students, and psychometrically sound measure of care is lacking. To fill this gap, we developed and validated the Chinese Care Scale (CCS). Integrating Chinese philosophies and traditions with Western caring theories, we framed care as a two-dimensional construct, comprising intrapersonal caring orientation and interpersonal caring behavior. Accordingly, we created and evaluated CCS across two studies. In Study 1, we developed an initial item pool of 26 items and assessed its content validity through an expert panel (N = 10). In Study 2, we evaluated the psychometric properties of the final 21-item CCS using a longitudinal sample of Chinese university students in Hong Kong (N = 963; two waves a year apart). Results demonstrated CCS’s time-invariant factor structure, excellent convergent, criterion-related, and discriminant validity, and high reliability. CCS scores predicted participants’ social-asset outcomes a year later, above and beyond a set of covariates, including multilevel contextual influences, demographics, and baseline outcome. CCS provides an objective tool for effectively measuring care in research and applied contexts among Chinese university students.
